request.spec:
A person can have plans: an amount, a start date, every N days (a whole number, at least 1) and an
end date, from a form on the row (PLAN_ADDED name=<name> amount=<amount> start=<date>
every=<n> end=<date>; an end before the start or a bad amount or interval is refused with an error
on the row). A generate button on the screen makes, for every plan on the sheet in the order they
were added, a DRAFT claim with the plan's amount for every plan date (the start, then every N days)
up to the end and the sheet's today that has none yet, dated that day with an empty note, by the
claim form's rules (a date the form refuses is skipped and tried again next time). Show how many
were made, and on each plan how many claims it has made so far.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person can have plans: an amount, a start date, every N days (a whole number, at least 1) and an
end date, from a form on the row (PLAN_ADDED name=<name> amount=<amount> start=<date>
every=<n> end=<date>; an end before the start or a bad amount or interval is refused with an error
on the row). A generate button on the screen makes, for every plan on the sheet in the order they
were added, a DRAFT claim with the plan's amount for every plan date (the start, then every N days)
up to the end and the sheet's today that has none yet, dated that day with an empty note, by the
claim form's rules (a date the form refuses is skipped and tried again next time). Show how many
were made, and on each plan how many claims it has made so far.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
People can now have plans, and a generate button makes their draft claims. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec, on the first run.

**Stored data** (`V73__person_plan.sql`)
- A new `person_plan` table holds each plan: its person, amount, start, every-N-days and end.
- A second table, `person_plan_date`, records each date a plan has already made a claim for. That is how "has none yet" is decided, and its row count is the "made so far" number shown on each plan.
- Both tables carry `sheet_id`, so the existing "view the sheet as of a date" feature picks them up automatically.

**Server** (new `plan` package, three endpoints)
- **Adding a plan:** `POST …/people/{personId}/plans` writes the `PLAN_ADDED` audit line in the order the test expects. It refuses (400) a bad amount (same rule as the claim form, so no negatives), an interval that isn't a whole number of at least 1, a bad date, or an end before the start.
- **Listing plans:** `GET …/plans` returns the sheet's plans in the order they were added, each with its count so far.
- **Generating:** `POST …/generate-plans` goes through the plans in the order they were added. For each plan date (the start, then every N days) up to the end and the sheet's today that has no claim yet, it makes a DRAFT claim dated that day with an empty note. It applies the same retirement and closed-period checks as pasted claims and writes the same records: claim log, `CLAIM_ADDED`, `LATE_ENTRY`, and rollup lines. A date those checks refuse is skipped and tried again next time. Archived sheets and viewers are refused, the same as for other changes.
- **Merge and transfer:** a merged person's plans move to the person they're merged into. A person transferred to another sheet loses their plans, the same as their other row data.

**Front end** (`features/plans/`)
- A "Plans" column on each person's row lists their plans with the "made" count and has the form to add one. Errors show in that row's `plan-error`.
- The "Generate plan claims" button sits after the paste box. It clears the old count on each press and shows the new count only after the claims and plans have been re-read.

Things I decided that you may want to check:
- **Blank start date:** it defaults to the sheet's today, following the from-date rule in `AGENTS.md`. The end date is required.
- **Sheet clone:** cloning a sheet does not copy its plans.
